The two perpendicular diameters intersect once, so they contribute \(1\) to \(I\).

---

A given diameter separates the four quadrants into two halves. Among the \(6\) possible pairs, exactly \(4\) have one endpoint on each side of that diameter, so

\[
P(\text{chord hits a given diameter})=\frac{4}{6}=\frac23.
\]

There are \(2\cdot 25=50\) diameter–chord pairs, so their expected contribution is

\[
50\cdot \frac23=\frac{100}{3}.
\]

---

### 3.  Two random chords intersect
Each chord chooses one of the \(6\) unordered quadrant pairs uniformly. Considering ordered pairs of chord types gives \(36\) equally likely cases.

Let the two chords have quadrant sets \(S\) and \(T\).

- **\(|S\cap T|=2\) (same pair, 6 cases):**  
  Both chords use the same two quadrants. They cross exactly when the orderings of the two endpoints in the first quadrant and in the second agree, which happens with probability \(\tfrac12\).

  The four endpoints occupy three consecutive quadrants, with two points in the shared quadrant. The chords cross exactly when those two shared points appear in one specific order, so the probability is again \(\tfrac12\).

- **\(S\cap T=\varnothing\), disjoint adjacent (4 cases):**  
  The chords lie in opposite semicircles, so they never cross: probability \(0\).

- **\(S\cap T=\varnothing\), disjoint opposite (2 cases):**  
  The endpoints must appear around the circle as \(S,T,S,T\); the chords always cross: probability \(1\).

Hence

\[
P(\text{two chords cross})=\frac{6\cdot\frac12+24\cdot\frac12+4\cdot0+2\cdot1}{36}
=\frac{3+12+2}{36}=\frac{17}{36}.

\[
300\cdot\frac{17}{36}=\frac{425}{3}.
\]

---

The expected number of interior intersections is

\[
\mathbb E[I]=1+\frac{100}{3}+\frac{425}{3}=1+\frac{525}{3}=1+175=176.
\]

Therefore

\[
\mathbb E[R]=28+\mathbb E[I]=28+176=204.
\]

(Equivalently, start from the \(4\) regions made by the diameters and add the \(25\) chords one by one; each new chord adds \(1\) plus its expected number of intersections with previous segments, yielding exactly the same total.)
